intervals.label: installation of DAMA/LIBRA
intervals.note: Start: 'fall 2002' (season: middle month with earliest/latest bounds). The 2008 apparatus paper says the installation started once DAMA/NaI completed its data taking in July 2002.
intervals.quote: whose installation is started at fall 2002;

intervals.label: first operations and test runs
intervals.note: 'DAMA/LIBRA has begun first operations in March 2003'; the first annual cycle used for the modulation analysis starts on 9 September 2003 (arXiv:1308.5109, Table 1).

intervals.label: second upgrade: all photomultipliers replaced (phase2)
intervals.note: Start: 'Fall 2010' (season bounds; the phase1 annual cycles end on 8 September 2010). End: the first phase2 cycle starts on 23 December 2010 (arXiv:1805.10486, Table 1). A first, smaller upgrade took place in September 2008, between the two last phase1 cycles.
intervals.quote: the second more important one has been carried out in Fall 2010

intervals.label: DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 commissioning (first annual cycle)
intervals.note: 'commissioning of phase2'; this first cycle is not used for the annual-modulation analysis. The LNGS page says the new measurements started in January 2011.

intervals.label: DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 annual cycles
intervals.note: Start: the second phase2 annual cycle begins on 2 November 2011 (arXiv:1805.10486, Table 1); the first six cycles run to 25 September 2017, eight cycles were released by 2021. End 2024: Conflict: the review (2026) says DAMA/LIBRA 'took data in two phases from 2003 to 2024' and a February 2026 LNGS seminar slide gives 'DAMA experiment (1995-2024)', whereas the DAMA page of LNGS (undated, listing publications up to 2023) says 'at present DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 is running'. The review's date is recorded, at year precision, with low confidence; the review also states that the DAMA/LIBRA detectors are now in the custody of INFN.

intervals.label: completed (data taking ended)
intervals.note: Year precision. Conflict: the review (2026) says DAMA/LIBRA 'took data in two phases from 2003 to 2024' and a February 2026 LNGS seminar slide gives 'DAMA experiment (1995-2024)', whereas the DAMA page of LNGS (undated, listing publications up to 2023) says 'at present DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 is running'. The review's date is recorded, at year precision, with low confidence; the review also states that the DAMA/LIBRA detectors are now in the custody of INFN.
intervals.quote: DAMA/LIBRA took data in two phases from 2003 to 2024.

crystal_count.quote: iii) the 25 highly radiopure NaI(Tl) detectors;

depth.note: Average depth of the Gran Sasso laboratory; the hall of the DAMA set-up is not given.
depth.quote: under 1,400 m of rock overburden, equivalent to an average depth of 3,800 meters of water equivalent (m.w.e.)

exposure.note: Cumulative exposure of DAMA/NaI, DAMA/LIBRA-phase1 and phase2 in the 2-6 keV region.
exposure.quote: the achieved C.L. for the full exposure (2.86 t x yr) is 13.7σ

target_mass.quote: The highly radiopure $\simeq$ 250 kg NaI(Tl) DAMA/LIBRA set-up is running at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory of the I.N.F.N.

threshold.note: Phase2 software energy threshold; phase1 used 2 keV.
threshold.quote: allowing the achievement of the software energy threshold at 1 keV

summary.plain: Twenty-five highly radiopure sodium iodide crystals, about 250 kg in all, read by photomultiplier tubes and shielded by copper, lead, polyethylene and concrete at Gran Sasso.
summary.technical: 25 NaI(Tl) detectors (9.70 kg each) in a 5x5 configuration, two PMTs each; phase1 PMTs replaced in 2010 by Hamamatsu R6233MOD PMTs (quantum efficiency 33-39% at 420 nm) for phase2, lowering the software threshold to 1 keV.

technology.quote: iii) the 25 highly radiopure NaI(Tl) detectors;
technology.value: Array of 25 highly radiopure NaI(Tl) scintillating crystals read by photomultiplier tubes
